And in the eleventh month of this year,
the Tatars returned again and came to the territory of Baghdad,
and reached as far as the place called Khaniqin.
And the forces of Baghdad went out
and encountered them.
And the Babylonians were routed,
and none of them was saved except three alone of the magnates,
while the rest were destroyed by the edge of the sword.
And the Tatars took great plunder,
and departed.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and fifty (1550 of the Greeks?):
which is the year 636 {OCR: 63c} of the Arabs:
the river Tigris overflowed,
and destroyed many quarters in Baghdad,
and sank two ships,
and about fifty persons were drowned.
And in the year after it,
nothing noteworthy happened in the regions near to us.
And in the year 1551,
1551 of the Greeks:
in the month of June,
the Tatars came,
and took captives from the land of the Iberians (Georgians) as far as the border of Erzurum.
And the forces of the Romans assembled and went to Armenia,
in order to prevent the Tatars from entering the territory of the Romans.
And when the Tatars heard that there was an assembly,
they left and returned to the land of the Scythians.
And the troops of the Romans remained there until winter,
and returned to their country.
And in that year Taj Bulgari,
the compounder of theriac, was sent as an ambassador from the Romans to Baghdad;
and he died there at the age of ninety years.
And in the year 1552,
1552 of the Greeks,
which is the year 638 {OCR: ܝܬܪܠܚ},
638 of the Arabs:
in the autumn season, an evil heresy broke out against the religion of the Arabs.
For an old Turkmen ascetic man whose name was Baba {OCR: Papa} appeared in the region of Amasya.
And he called himself "Rasul",
that is to say, "Apostle".
For he said
that he was in truth the apostle of God,
and that Muhammad was an impostor and not an apostle.
And a great multitude of Turkmens joined him,
and believed in him through the illusions which he showed them.
And he sent a man from among his disciples whose name was Baba Ishaq to the region of Hisn Mansur,
which is the border of the territory of the Romans,
so that he might make disciples from there on his way.
This man, when he came,
captivated many with devotion to his master.
And he prepared for himself weapons of war,
and all the Turkmen peasants joined him;
and they sold their donkeys, their oxen, and their sheep,
and bought horses for themselves and mounted them.
